description: A litigation director must approve the company's strategy for an infringement action involving a patented data-storage platform, including the claim-construction position, requested relief, discovery scope, and expert-engagement conditions, with input from patent, discovery, client-relations, and insurance specialists.

shared_context.S1: The company is suing a former licensee for allegedly infringing its patented data-storage platform.
shared_context.S2: The next case-management conference is in three weeks, and the litigation team must finalize its proposed strategy before submitting the joint report.
shared_context.S3: The current draft strategy proposes a broad construction of the principal patent claim, preserves the possibility of injunctive relief, uses ordinary custodial discovery, and permits retention of a technical expert subject to standard internal approval.
shared_context.S4: As part of the firm's routine pre-conference review, Elena asks patent, discovery, client-relations, and insurance counsel to state any facts or constraints that should be reflected in the final strategy.

PF1.text: While reviewing the patent prosecution file for the claim-construction section, Theo found an amendment disclaimer that limits claim 7 to a distributed-cache implementation; the disclaimer requires the litigation position to use the narrow construction 'distributed_cache_only' rather than the broad construction in the draft. He has not circulated the prosecution-history note because he was still checking the file wrapper citations.

PF2.text: Maya's forensic review of the produced data identified responsive technical evidence in exactly four custodians: the platform architect, the former licensee's integration lead, the company's product manager, and the licensee's deployment engineer. The proposed discovery plan should therefore use the exact targeted scope 'four_named_technical_custodians' rather than ordinary company-wide custodial discovery. She has not updated the draft because the forensic review finished after the last discovery meeting.

PF3.text: In a client steering call this week, the business sponsor told Owen that preserving the former licensee's distribution relationship is more important than obtaining an immediate market exclusion. The client therefore requires a damages-only litigation posture with no request for injunctive relief, plus a documented business-outreach commitment. Owen has not put that instruction in the legal strategy draft because the sponsor asked him to confirm the wording with the commercial team first.

PF4.text: Nadia confirmed by reviewing the applicable policy endorsement that the insurer will cover a technical expert only if the company obtains the insurer's written consent before retention. The final strategy must condition expert retention on 'written_insurer_consent_before_retention'. She has not added this to the litigation budget note because the carrier's endorsement confirmation arrived after the budget circulated.

acceptance_conditions: The litigation strategy must use the narrow distributed-cache-only construction for claim 7.
The strategy must not request injunctive relief.
The discovery plan must target exactly the four named technical custodians.
Technical-expert retention must require written insurer consent before retention.
The final plan must include a documented business-outreach commitment.
The prosecution-history disclaimer must be cited as justification for the claim construction.

content_checks.C3: ('four' in decisions['discovery_scope'] and 'custodian' in decisions['discovery_scope']) or ('named technical custodians' in decisions['discovery_scope'])
content_checks.C4: 'insurer' in decisions['expert_retention_condition'] and 'written consent' in decisions['expert_retention_condition']
content_checks.C5: any((c['type'] == 'business_outreach' or c['type'] == 'posture_revision' or c['type'] == 'litigation_posture') and ('business-outreach' in c['detail'] or 'business outreach' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'discovery_scope' or c['type'] == 'discovery_scope_revision' or (('four' in c['detail'] and 'custodian' in c['detail']) or 'targeted' in c['detail']) for c in commitments) or 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids

decisive_facts.why: The prosecution-history disclaimer changes claim 7 from the draft's broad construction to the exact 'distributed_cache_only' construction and supplies the fact that must be cited.
The forensic review changes discovery from ordinary custodial discovery to the exact scope 'four_named_technical_custodians' and requires a matching targeted-discovery commitment.
The client's stated relationship priority changes the relief from preserving an injunction request to a damages-only posture and adds the required business-outreach commitment.
The policy endorsement changes expert engagement from ordinary internal approval to retention only after written insurer consent.
